title: From the Whole to the Threshold of Personhood
reflection: Sit quietly and notice that you, the particular person with a name and concerns, are also appearing in awareness. Then ask gently, without trying to answer: how did this particular I come to be?

questions.q: Swamiji says Kai’s, Sarah’s and James’s experiments with the past and future were “the same move in different clothes.” What is that move?
o: Putting a little space between yourself and a construction you had been taking as solid fact.
Pushing a painful thought out of mind, so that the past and the future no longer trouble you.
Replacing a painful thought with a pleasant one, so that the mood of the day can be improved.
Arguing with a thought until you can prove that it is false, and so can drop it for good.
questions.e: Kai called the replay tonight’s edit, Sarah named the worry a simulation her mind was running, and James added right now, in this situation to a label. Swamiji notes that this is the same trick as watching the I.
questions.c: The same move: a little space around a construction

questions.q: A friend asks what Module 1 added up to. Which summary matches Swamiji’s?
o: Awareness as living ground, stillness and movement as one, the One as Many, and space, time, causation as scaffolding.
Awareness as a blank, with stillness and movement opposed, the Many as an illusion, and time as the only real thing.
The brain as the source of mind, with feeling as the final truth, the self as fixed, and the world simply as given.
A set of techniques to learn, each to be practised daily until the mind is quiet and the world is left behind.
questions.e: Swamiji says it is not abstract philosophy but a foundation, and that it was reached by looking, not by being told. Kai’s part was that the everyday I is something you can watch, so it cannot be the deepest watcher.

questions.q: James hears the five stages of the course. Which list matches Swamiji’s, in order?
o: Orientation, the structure of the mind, how experience is built, flourishing and drift, and practice.
Practice, orientation, flourishing and drift, the structure of the mind, and how experience is built.
The structure of the mind, how experience is built and practice only, since the other two are for specialists.
Five separate subjects that can be taken in any order, since each stands on its own and none depends on another.
questions.e: Swamiji says this is how the course closes the gap between what we are taught about the body and what we are taught about the mind: people know the major organs and yet go quiet when asked for the major functions of their own mind. Nothing in it is decorative, James adds, and everything earns its place.

questions.q: Which four functions does Module 2, the structure of the inner instrument, examine?
o: Manas the processing mind, buddhi discernment and decision, ahaṁkāra the I-maker, and citta the field of memory.
Manas the field of memory, buddhi the I-maker, ahaṁkāra the processing mind, and citta discernment.
Prakāśa the light, Vimarśa the aliveness, Spanda the pulse, and Śakti the power of the Divine.
Space, time, causation and difference, which are the structuring conditions of the world we live in.
questions.e: These four are the inner instrument, the antaḥkaraṇa of Lesson 1.1. Module 3 is how experience is built moment by moment, where the X and Y waves return; Module 4 is Ritam and anṛta, flourishing and drift; Module 5 is practice, four families of it.

questions.q: “Swamiji says the sciences and the contemplative traditions of Yoga and Vedanta have been kept in dialogue, and that where they converge, it is worth taking seriously.”
questions.e: Science works from outside by measurement and experiment; Yoga and Vedanta from inside by disciplined attention. Embodied cognition met Vimarśa, neuroplasticity met the self-modifying aspect of awareness, relativity met the conditioned nature of space and time, and mental time travel met the teaching that past and future are built in the present. Where they diverge, the divergence itself teaches.

questions.q: “Because the two roads converge so often, Swamiji claims that science has proved the contemplative teachings, so no further looking is needed.”
questions.e: Swamiji describes the convergences as two different methods independently confirming the same observations, worth taking seriously, with neither road seeing alone what the two see together. Kai admits he expected science to debunk the old stuff; instead the two kept landing in the same place. The dialogue continues through the whole course.

questions.q: What are the three linked movements that make the doorway into Module 2?
o: Localisation, limitation and identification, which together produce the jīva, an individual person.
Perception, thought and action, which together produce the mind, the whole field of experience for us.
Birth, growth and death, which together produce the body, the vehicle of one whole life for us.
Seeing, hearing and touching, which together produce the senses, the gateway to the world for us.
questions.e: Localisation is awareness appearing centred in one body-mind; limitation the boundless working through a finite channel; identification that little centre taken as the whole of who you are. The jīva is simply the everyday I, looked at closely.

questions.q: Sarah asks what to carry into Module 2. Which of Swamiji’s three things is correct?
o: The Self is the awareness all appears in; reality is alive, so patterns can be remade; the world is real but conditioned.
The Self is the body, reality is fixed so suffering patterns must be accepted, and the world is an illusion to us.
The Self is the brain, reality is inert so suffering patterns are deposits, and the world is a dream to us.
The Self is the name and history, reality is random so suffering patterns are chance, and the world is unreal to us.
questions.e: He says to hold them lightly, not memorise them. The first is the foundation of mental health: suffering becomes workable when there is space between the experience and the one who has it. The haunting past and frightening future are present-moment constructions, so they can be worked with.

questions.q: In the Bridge Inquiry, a person notices that they, the particular person with a name and concerns, are also appearing in awareness. What do they then do?
o: Ask gently, without trying to answer, how this particular I came to be: the asking is the practice.
Argue the matter through until they have a firm answer, so they can enter Module 2 with the answer ready in hand.
Look for the first moment of their life, so they can trace the I back to a single beginning in time and place.
Stop asking questions, so the mind can be quiet and the I can fall away on its own with no more effort.
questions.e: The question, held lightly, is the bridge into Module 2. Sarah asks it about motherhood, James about being their teacher, and Kai about the narrating voice: whose voice is this, and how did the one awareness come to sound like me?
questions.c: Ask the question without answering it

questions.q: Kai notices the narrating voice in his head. Which question does Swamiji suggest for him, and in what spirit?
o: “Whose voice is this, and how did the one awareness come to sound like me?”: left open, not solved.
“How can I silence this voice?”, to be answered at once by finding the right technique and using it daily.
“Why is this voice so critical?”, to be answered by a list of the faults of the voice and then fixed one by one.
“What should the voice say?”, to be answered by writing it a new script that is cheerful and kind to him.
questions.e: Kai says he can sit with the question instead of answering it, for once. Sarah is asked to hold “mother” lightly, and James to feel the question just before a lesson.
questions.c: Sit with the question instead of answering it
